title: An unattended epic absorbs the defects it discovers
description:
OPERATOR, 2026-09-22: 'for an unattended software factory, discovered defects related to the epic should be absorbed and fixed as part of the epic' — 'it's designed to work unattended'.

THE CONTRADICTION, in the system's own words. ticfac findings ends its listing with:

    4 finding(s), 4 waiting for a person; the epic's close-out does not
    hand over while a finding is untriaged.

A factory that runs unattended cannot have a step whose only actor is a person. Today
every finding a worker drafts stops the close-out until someone types one of three
verdicts. This session hit it four times in one epic, and three of the four were
defects IN THE GROUND THE EPIC WAS STANDING ON - two fixtures that made the gate red at
base, and a model-name mismatch that would have refused a container boot. An
unattended run would have stopped on all of them.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, so this is not started from nothing:
  - Findings are drafted durably on the run branch and survive a restart.
  - Triage has three verdicts: --promote-as <tick>, --discard, --fixed-as <commit>.
    her already added 'fixed in this epic' as a verdict; aqm already moved the
    untriaged gate from every tick to the close-out.
  - A promoted finding becomes a tick, which is the absorption MECHANISM. What is
    missing is the DECISION, which today only a person can make.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is a judgement rather than a mechanism:

  1. THE CRITERION, and it is the operator's and it is MECHANICAL (2026-09-22):
     'if the finding is gating the epic's goal it should be absorbed.'

     Not 'is it related', which is prose about prose and needs a judgement. The test is
     whether the epic's DEFINITION OF DONE can be demonstrated while the finding stands.
     If it cannot, the finding is gating the goal and the epic absorbs it. If it can,
     the finding is a backlog tick with an owner, however interesting it is.

     This is why every epic wants a goal-compatible done - checkable, bounded,
     outside-in. The done is not decoration here; it is the FUNCTION that decides
     absorption, and an epic whose done is prose cannot run this test at all. An epic
     with no stated done should refuse to absorb rather than guess, and say so.

     Worked from this session, which is where the criterion came from:
       gate red at base (two fixtures)     GATING - xte's done requires a cloud epic
                                           run, and no tick can close behind a red gate
       model spelled two ways (qu3)        GATING - the done says a run dispatches on
                                           the gateway model; the boot would refuse it
       merge_failed names no file (ky5)    NOT GATING - painful, cost an hour of mine,
                                           and the epic's done is reachable with it
                                           standing. Backlog, and it stayed backlog.

  1b. WHERE THE MECHANICAL TEST CANNOT REACH, AND A CLASSIFIER EARNS ITS PLACE
     (operator, 2026-09-22: 'are there still scenarios where an llm classifier is
     useful to determine if a discovered issue gates the definition of done? i would
     imagine yes' - and the answer is yes, in one specific place).

     Running the done is an ORACLE only for acceptance items that are RUNNABLE NOW. Two
     cases defeat it, and the second is the common one:

       - The item cannot be checked yet because the epic has not built the thing it is
         about. xte's done requires a cloud epic run dispatching into per-tick
         sandboxes. Mid-epic there is no such dispatch to run. Nothing can go red.

       - THE FINDING IS ITSELF A PREDICTION. qu3, the best finding of this session, is
         exactly this: 'when s45 wires the table's value into a cloud dispatch, a value
         routed into a container boot will be refused'. Nothing was red. No test failed.
         The finding's own text says why: 'nothing in this tick's Go tests can catch it
         because no test boots a container'. Deciding it gates the done means reasoning
         about prose against prose - which is precisely what a classifier is for, and
         precisely what running something cannot do.

     So the shape is TWO-TIER, not classifier-instead-of-test:
       - The done runs where it can run. That verdict is AUTHORITATIVE and no classifier
         overrides it.
       - Where the item is not yet runnable, the classifier PREDICTS, with confidence,
         and the absorption is recorded as predicted rather than observed.

     ERR TOWARD ABSORBING, because the costs are not symmetric. A false positive costs
     the epic some work it did not need. A false negative closes an epic whose goal is
     unmet, in a factory where nobody is watching - the failure this whole epic exists
     to prevent. The threshold belongs on the cheap side.

     The question to ask is a Choice over THIS EPIC'S OWN ACCEPTANCE ITEMS plus 'none',
     which is a closed enum per epic and is Jev's sweet spot - and it answers gvc's
     other requirement for free, that an absorption names which acceptance item was
     unreachable.

     AND IT IS SELF-MEASURING, which wne's dataset could not be: every finding that is
     predicted and then LATER becomes runnable gives a labelled pair - what the
     classifier said, what the done actually did. That is a calibration set the factory
     generates by operating, rather than one anybody has to build.

  2. ABSORPTION MUST BE BOUNDED, or an epic never ends - but the criterion in (1)
     already does most of the bounding, because only goal-gating defects absorb and a
     goal is finite. What remains is the recursion: a defect discovered while fixing an
     absorbed defect, which may itself gate the goal. Depth and wall clock are the
     candidate bounds; pick one and make exceeding it the thing that stops for a person,
     so the stop is rare and meaningful rather than routine.
  3. THE EPIC'S SHAPE CHANGES MID-RUN. Absorbing means adding ticks and waves to a
     running epic. Axiom 1 applies: the absorbed tick and the reasoning that absorbed it
     must be recorded on the run branch, so a cold re-derivation reaches the same epic
     rather than a smaller one.
  4. THE DEFINITION OF DONE MUST STILL MEAN SOMETHING. An epic that absorbs freely can
     drift until it is no longer the epic anyone asked for. The absorbed work is in
     service of the stated done, not an extension of it, and the close-out retro should
     be able to say what was absorbed and why.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: a finding that is genuinely out of scope still becomes a backlog
tick with an owner, and the ceiling still bounds everything. Unattended means nobody has
to be there, not that nobody is ever told.
acceptance_criteria:
[A1] An epic run that discovers a defect gating its own definition of done absorbs it as a tick, fixes it and closes, with no person triaging.
[A2] A finding the done is reachable without becomes a backlog tick with an owner instead.
[A3] Where an acceptance item is runnable, running it is the authoritative verdict and no classifier overrides it.
[A4] Where an item is not yet runnable, a classified prediction decides and is recorded as a prediction, distinguishable from an observation.
[A5] The absorption names which acceptance item was unreachable and is recorded on the run branch, so a cold re-derivation reaches the same epic.
[A6] An epic with no stated done refuses to absorb rather than guessing, and says so.
[A7] The recursion is bounded, and exceeding the bound is what stops for a person.
[A8] A prediction whose item later becomes runnable is scored against what the done actually did, and the close-out retro reports what was absorbed, against which acceptance item, and whether it was predicted or observed.
